items.title: Andy Taylor, Duran Duran Guitarist, Dies at 65
items.summary:
Andy Taylor, the guitarist whose playing shaped Duran Duran's run of early-1980s hits, died Monday at his home of prostate cancer, surrounded by his family. He was 65. Taylor had lived with stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer since his diagnosis in 2018.

His wife, Tracey, said in a statement shared with Variety on behalf of the family, "To the world, Andy was a brilliant guitarist, but to us, he was the most wonderful husband, a loving dad and the proudest grandfather. He was the rock of our family." Duran Duran, in its own statement, described him as the member who "brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music" from the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East, and credited his dry wit and "no-nonsense outlook on life" with keeping the band grounded.

Taylor was a 19-year-old from Northumberland, fresh off touring British army bases with cover bands, when he answered an April 1980 Melody Maker classified seeking a "Live Wire Guitarist." As he wrote in his 2008 memoir "Wild Boy," the ad named Mick Ronson and Steve Jones as touchstones, "so I thought it looked worth a call." Eight months after he joined the lineup, EMI signed the band.

What followed was one of the decade's steepest commercial climbs. "Girls on Film" reached No. 5 in the U.K. and lifted the self-titled debut to No. 3; 1982's "Rio" produced "Hungry Like the Wolf" and its title track, and "Is There Something I Should Know" gave the group its first U.K. No. 1 in 1983. Three singles reached the U.S. top five across 1982 and 1983, helped enormously by MTV airplay of videos directed by Russell Mulcahy and by Kevin Godley and Lol Creme.

Those clips, shot in Sri Lanka and Antigua among other places, won the band both of its Grammys in 1986, for best short form and best long form music video. Taylor remembered the shoots as hazardous as well as lucrative: "Several of us risked being drowned, we narrowly escaped being trampled by a crazed elephant, and we were forced to flee one shoot after being threatened by four thousand angry monks." By 1984, as "The Reflex" and "The Wild Boys" topped charts on both sides of the Atlantic, the band's cocaine use had become tabloid material, something Taylor later confirmed.

Taylor declined to attend Duran Duran's induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in November 2022, citing his health. "Although my current condition is not immediately life-threatening there is no cure," he said at the time, describing a setback that followed a period of life-extending treatment. He is survived by Tracey and their family.

items.title: Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade Postponed To Saturday Due To Severe Weather; NBC Will Rerun 2025 Parade On Thursday
items.summary:
Macy's, NBC and the city of New York have pushed the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday, Nov. 28, citing a storm expected to hit the city Thursday morning. In place of a live broadcast, NBC will rerun last year's parade Thursday at 8:30 a.m. in all time zones.

"Due to the extreme weather conditions, the city of New York, Macy's and NBC have decided, in the interest of safety for both the participants and spectators, to move the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday, Nov. 28," the network said in a statement, adding that more details would follow.

The forecast driving the decision is a nor'easter forming late Wednesday and strengthening Thursday as it moves toward the Atlantic. AccuWeather projects one to two inches of rain in New York, with sustained winds of 12 to 25 mph and gusts reaching 30 mph that build through the day. Deadline reported Tuesday that NBC had been tracking the system closely, with its coverage set to run Thursday from 8:30 a.m. to noon ET on the network and Peacock.

The timing is awkward for everyone involved, since this is the parade's 100th edition. Macy's had planned 100 of its signature large balloons and an "All-Star Broadway Thanksgiving Day Celebration," a 10-minute medley featuring performers from current and long-running Broadway shows.

The parade has gone dark before, canceled in 1942, 1943 and 1944 during World War II and reduced to a television-only event staged outside the Herald Square store in 2020. The balloons have been grounded only once, in 1971, for a similar combination of rain and wind. Last year's broadcast drew 34.3 million viewers across NBC and Peacock, the largest combined audience the parade has recorded.

items.title: Michael Giles, King Crimson’s Founding Drummer, Dead at 84
items.summary:
Michael Giles, the drummer who co-founded King Crimson and played on the band's debut album, died Monday at 84. The band confirmed his death in a statement posted to its website.

In that statement, King Crimson credited Giles with an "extraordinary rhythmic imagination, musical sensitivity and highly inventive approach to drumming" that the group called fundamental to its pioneering sound. Consequence reported the news on Tuesday.

Giles started the band in 1968 with Robert Fripp, Greg Lake, Ian McDonald and lyricist Peter Sinfield. He drummed on 1969's "In the Court of the Crimson King," the album that effectively launched British progressive rock, then announced his departure soon after its release, uneasy with how quickly the band had become famous and with where its music was heading.

He still contributed to the follow-up, 1970's "In the Wake of Poseidon," before moving on to other work. That included a collaborative project with McDonald and session drumming for Steve Winwood, Bryan Ferry, Kevin Ayers and Lake.

Later in his career, Giles co-founded The 21st Century Schizoid Band, which brought together several early King Crimson members to play material from the group's first years.
